output.summary: A large pine native to eastern North America, eastern white pine has flexible bluish-green needles usually bundled in fives. Mature trees can live for centuries and tower over mixed forests. During winter starvation, Algonquian peoples dried and pounded the inner bark into flour; Ojibwe people also stewed young male cones with meat, and the seeds are sweet and nutritious.
